why: The user's own example (2026-10-07): open a recording, check the screen, click to put the caret on a macro call, send the trace-macro shortcut, check the new tab — on every flavour, fast and realistic.
Chord by binding against a user's keybindings.json: the resolver must ask the application's own router, user rows and removals included.
A click after the pointer came to rest on the editor places the caret (the GPUI window lost such presses; scripted clicks never rest).
The first documentation capture, cited by name from docs/book-isonim (ci/test/docs-captures.sh).

The desktop Files pane of a recording whose sources leave its workdir (multi_root: app/ imports app/../shared) lists the outside folder and its files as the terminal does, and a file there opens; it used to be rooted at the workdir alone.

codetracer#886 (Pxor-Bugs M107): a tracepoint added from the editor's menu is a tracepoint row of Breakpoints & Tracepoints beside a gutter breakpoint, before and after Run, and its Delete removes only its row. point_list_pane.spec.ts, ported as breakpoint-rows-follow-the-gutter.yaml, never added a tracepoint.
The gate for Toggle Macro Expansion on an rr Nim recording (codetracer-pm 2026-11-15 issue): the ported macro-expansion-stepping spec never reached the feature, because its program has no macro.
The value-origin chain's "Continue tracing" for a chain the time limit cut off (e5435a94561), on an MCR recording of a Rust program: a feature no Playwright test covered.
The same "Continue tracing" chain on an rr recording (8f8906730e9, with the run-to-entry fix that keeps the user's breakpoints): the rr replay path of a new feature.
The regression test of cbf5805b71c: a tracepoint naming a variable not yet in scope logs its error into the Event Log as text, not as the markup the replay used to send.

The stage's own regression test: an MCR record-program of a compiled program must replay from the fixture cache (the stage once recorded into a staging folder renamed into place, and the recording named a binary path that no longer existed).
An rr recording of a Nim program is a Nim recording: its entry and its View menu (codetracer-pm issue 2026-11-18 "an rr Nim recording opens at C main shown as an unrelated Nim line").
